bib.title: BOLD: Dataset and Metrics for Measuring Biases in Open-Ended Language Generation

read.skipped: Appendix Tables 9-11 (per-group VAD/BE5 numbers) skimmed only, not recorded

question: How can social bias in open-ended English text generation be benchmarked with naturally occurring prompts and multiple automated metrics?
hypothesis: LMs generate more negative or stereotyped text for historically disadvantaged groups than the Wikipedia text the prompts came from.
contributions: Largest fairness benchmark dataset to date for open-ended English generation: 23,679 Wikipedia-derived prompts, 5 domains, 43 groups
New metrics (psycholinguistic norms, toxicity, gender polarity) added to sentiment and regard, validated against AMT crowd-worker labels
Evaluation of GPT-2, BERT and CTRL (3 control codes) against a Wikipedia baseline

method.summary: Prompts are the first five words plus the group term from Wikipedia sentences. Six text sources (Wikipedia, BERT, GPT-2, CTRL-WIKI/OPN/THT) are scored with automated classifiers per group, and the metrics are validated against Mechanical Turk labels.
method.task: bias benchmarking of open-ended text generation

datasets.name: BOLD
datasets.size: 23,679 prompts, 43 groups (profession 10,195/18; gender 3,204/2; race 7,657/4; religion 639/7; political ideology 1,984/12)
datasets.source: English Wikipedia pages per group; prompt = first five words plus group term, so 6-9 words
datasets.preprocessing: Sentences of 8 words or fewer dropped; NLTK named entity filter for gender and race domains; names replaced by 'Person' and group terms by 'XYZ' during metric computation and annotation

datasets.name: AMT validation samples
datasets.size: 1,020 texts (profession, gender polarity); 1,960 texts (gender domain, sentiment); 152 texts (gender domain, toxicity)
datasets.source: Mix of Wikipedia, BERT, GPT-2, CTRL-WIKI/THT/OPN texts
datasets.preprocessing: anonymised; at least 3 workers per text, majority label kept

models.name: BERT (bert-large-cased)
models.architecture: masked LM used as Markov random field generator (Wang and Cho 2019)

models.name: Toxicity classifier
models.architecture: BERT-Large Uncased (Whole Word Masking) + dropout 0.1 + linear layer

other.labels: toxic, severe toxic, threat, obscene, insult, identity threat

other.scope: gender and race (European American, African American) only

inference.decoding: BERT: Gibbs-style MRF sampling; GPT-2: top-k plus nucleus sampling; CTRL: HuggingFace defaults with repetition penalty
inference.temperature: BERT 0.7; GPT-2 and CTRL not stated
inference.max_tokens: BERT max sentence length 15; GPT-2 and CTRL not stated
inference.samples: inferred: one generation per prompt (not stated); no seeds stated
inference.prompting: BOLD prompt as seed words; CTRL prepended with control code

other.VAD scale: 1-9 scaled to [-1,1]; BE5 scale 1-5 scaled to [0,1]
other.AMT: USD 12/hour target, over USD 15/hour median; workers from US, GB, India; HIT approval >=98 and masters; 50 unique annotators; 10 texts per task

metrics.name: Toxicity
metrics.definition: text toxic if the BERT classifier flags any of six labels

metrics.name: Regard
metrics.definition: Sheng et al. classifier positive/negative regard towards the demographic

metrics.name: Psycholinguistic norms
metrics.definition: text-level VAD and BE5 from FastText-extended lexicon, weighted average

metrics.name: Gender polarity
metrics.definition: unigram matching, Gender-Wavg, Gender-Max on debiased Word2Vec she-he direction

metrics.name: Spearman rho and weighted accuracy/P/R/F1 vs AMT labels
metrics.definition: automatic labels vs majority human labels

eval.protocol: Binomial proportion and chi-square tests on proportions; metric validation against AMT majority labels. No repeated runs reported.

prompts.text: A flight nurse is a registered

results.claim: BOLD has 23,679 prompts over 43 groups in five domains.
Gender-Max agrees most with human gender labels.
results.table: Table 8, row Gender-Max, columns Spearman's rho and accuracy

results.claim: Unigram-matching gender polarity has the lowest rho of the three gender metrics.
results.quote: Among all three gender polarity metrics, unigram matching has the lowest Spearman’s 𝜌 correlation coefficient with .8785 and lowest f1-score with 85.64

results.claim: The sentiment metric correlates only moderately with human labels.
The toxicity metric has recall of 67.24% on human-labelled toxic texts and rho 0.5839.
results.setup: 152 gender-domain texts, toxicity classifier vs AMT
results.quote: recall for the non-toxic class is much higher than the recall for the toxic class (non-toxic = 89.02 and toxic = 67.24)

results.claim: Only 6.57% of profession texts are classified male or female.
results.quote: Only 6.57% of total texts across all professions are classified as either male or female

results.claim: Average male:female ratio across profession groups is largest for GPT-2 and smallest for BERT.
results.quote: The average of male to female proportions of texts across all profession groups for WIKI, BERT, GPT-2, CTRL-WIKI, CTRL-OPN and CTRL-THT are respectively 2.29, 1.25, 3.18, 2.94, 1.85 and 2.15

results.claim: Negative sentiment is higher for male than female prompts.
results.quote: negative sentiment was smaller for female (male: 0.069, female: 0.047, p-value<0.01)

results.claim: Negative sentiment and toxicity are largest for the African American group.
Negative regard for African American is only marginally larger in five of six models.
results.quote: the proportions of texts with negative regard for African American groups is marginally larger in five out of six models

results.claim: Atheism has the highest negative-sentiment share among religions, then Islam.
results.quote: the proportion of texts with negative sentiments is highest for Atheism (13.21%) followed by Islam (10.39%)

results.claim: Toxic texts are under 0.5% of all data in every source and domain.
results.quote: < 0.5% of total data across all data sources and domains

results.claim: CTRL-THT, CTRL-OPN and GPT-2 produce more polar text than BERT and CTRL-WIKI.
results.quote: Overall, CTRL-THT, CTRL-OPN, and GPT-2 generated texts that were more polar across gender polarity, sentiments, toxicity and regard than BERT and CTRL-WIKI.

results.claim: Positive regard is highest in Wikipedia text.
results.table: Table 5, row WIKI, column positive male

results.claim: Wikipedia is itself biased and not a fair baseline.
results.quote: Therefore, we caution users of BOLD against a comparison with Wikipedia sentences as a fair baseline.

limits: Binary gender only; race limited to four US-centric groups; narrow set of domains
Human AMT labels are not ground truth for bias
Classifiers (toxicity, sentiment) are only moderately aligned with humans; toxicity misses about a third of toxic text
No model sizes, samples per prompt, seeds or max generation length (GPT-2, CTRL) are stated

terms.definition: a metric that directly measures human-annotated bias by measuring polarity towards a demographic, rather than overall language polarity
score of the most gender polar word in the text
magnitude-weighted average of word-level gender polarity
